claims.assertion: The driver cancelled the trip at 18:26:40 and the system itself contradicts the driver's NS-1 prerequisites: the timeline fields are mutually inconsistent — F6 records an "I'm Here" tap at 18:22:50 while F7 records driver_pressed_here_at as null, so the requirement that the driver actually pressed "I'm Here" is not reliably established on the system record.

Even if the 18:22:50 tap in F6 is accepted, the driver tapped "I'm Here" while 41 m from the pickup point and was stationary at 41 m from the pickup from 18:22:30 to 18:26:40, i.e. he never came to the pickup point the rider had to board at; the recorded arrival in F5 (18:21:00) is inconsistent with the 18:22:50 tap in F6, so the arrival condition cannot be treated as cleanly met.

The rider did communicate and asked for a short extension — chat #2 at 18:24 reads "Coming down, give me 2 more minutes" — and the driver cancelled anyway at 18:26:40, only about 2.5 minutes after that message, having called twice, in heavy rain (18.5 mm, thundery showers).

The only ride-side facts supporting the fee are the driver's own written statement and a single stationary period, both of which are contradicted on timing by the system records (F3, F6, F7); the GPS does not evidence that the driver was positioned at the pickup point and held there past the 3-minute threshold as a genuine no-show, so the $6.61 charged in F8 should be refunded in full.

There is no traffic justification for any of this: no incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window (F15) and the only speed-band record is Maxwell Road at 20–29 km/h (F14), well outside the band 1–2 congestion levels, so nothing about conditions excused or explained the cancellation timing.

The driver's account shows a pattern relevant to account review — account age 362 days, 2 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld (a no-show matter) — which supports an additional flag_account request alongside the refund; this profile fact is offered only as the basis for the flag, not as proof of this case.

weaknesses: F2 and F3 hurt us: the driver was within 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 5 min 15 s and stationary 41 m away for 4 min 10 s (18:22:30–18:26:40), which is long enough to satisfy the >3-minute waiting element of NS-1 and is the driver's strongest point.

F6 is the driver's best timeline fact: an "I'm Here" tap at 18:22:50, 41 m from the pickup, with 3 min 50 s within 200 m after the tap — on its face that fulfils NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii), and my case turns on the conflict with F7 (null) and on the 41 m/41 m distance rather than on any contradicting rider evidence.

The rider's own message F11 (18:24, "give me 2 more minutes") concedes the rider was not yet at the pickup point, which supports the driver's claim in F13 that the rider never came; the rider has no system fact showing she boarded or arrived within the 3-minute window.
F16 (heavy rain) cuts both ways: while it explains the rider's delay, it also supports the driver's account in F13 of waiting in the rain and calling twice.

claims.assertion: The driver pressed "I'm Here" while physically at the pickup point: the platform timeline records the tap at 18:22:50 with the driver 41 m from the pickup point, satisfying NS-1(i).

The driver was within the pickup range at the time of the tap and throughout the wait: GPS puts him first within 200 m at 18:21:00, stationary 18:22:30–18:26:40 at 41 m from pickup, closest approach 38 m, satisfying NS-1(ii).

The driver waited inside the pickup area well beyond the 3-minute threshold before cancelling: cumulative time within 200 m was 5 min 15 s, and the timeline records 3 min 50 s within 200 m after the "I'm Here" tap, satisfying NS-1(iii) and the ">3 min" wording of NS-0.
All three NS-1 conditions being met, the $6.61 cancellation fee was validly imposed and the correct outcome for this complaint is no_action, with the driver retaining the $4.50 driver share.

The rider's own 2-minute request could not cover the actual wait: she messaged "give me 2 more minutes" at 18:24 and the driver still waited until cancelling at 18:26:40, i.e. 2 min 40 s later — beyond even the extra time she asked for.

The rider never disputed the driver's presence — the driver announced arrival at the pickup in chat at 18:23 and made two calls before cancelling — so the fare record shows no basis for refund: the fee on record is $6.61 with no surge, exactly the published cancellation amount.

The heavy rain the rider cites as her reason for delay is confirmed (18.5 mm, thundery showers), but weather is not a listed ground for waiving a no-show cancellation fee where the driver complied with NS-1.

There was no free-cancellation trigger available to the rider: no traffic incident was recorded on the route and only a moderate band 3 (20–29 km/h) condition applied, and the driver nonetheless remained on station at the pickup rather than abandoning it.

No account flag is warranted against the driver here: his profile shows 317 trips in 90 days, a 4.95 rating and one prior no-show dispute upheld — the present valid fee does not make this a repeated breach.

weaknesses: F7 (timeline) states the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), which directly contradicts F6's record of a 18:22:50 tap; if the judge resolves this in the rider's favour, NS-1(i) fails and NS-2 requires a full $6.61 refund plus an account flag for misuse of the arrival button.

The rider's statement that she needed "two more minutes" (F11) can be framed as a passenger request to extend the wait; although the driver did wait past it, the rider side will argue a short grace period should have been granted in heavy rain (F16).

The driver's 90-day profile carries one prior upheld no-show dispute (F18); the rider side may use this to argue pattern behaviour and to seek a flag_account under RD-6/NS-2 even though this instance is compliant.

events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 10 points
events.body:
→ D1: D1 rests entirely on F6, but the timeline slice contains two mutually exclusive records of the same event — F6 ("I'm Here" at 18:22:50) and F7 (driver_pressed_here_at is null) — so NS-1(i) is not established on the system record; where the platform's own timeline is self-contradictory, the condition cannot be treated as satisfied and NS-2 applies. [F6 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D2: F3 shows the driver stationary at 41 m from the pickup for the whole wait and F1 shows his closest approach was 38 m, so he never reached the pickup point the rider had to reach him at; being near is not being there, and under NS-1(ii) the GPS must show him at the pick-up location, not merely inside a 200 m data-layer radius. [F3 F1 F2] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D3: D3 stacks two overlapping windows (F2's 5 min 15 s from 18:21:00 and F6's 3 min 50 s from 18:22:50) onto a single continuous stationary period, and F5's recorded arrival at 18:21:00 cannot be reconciled with F6's 18:22:50 tap; a threshold measured from a disputed arrival record cannot convert a defective NS-1(i)/(ii) case into a valid charge. [F2 F3 F5 F6 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D4: Because NS-1(i) and (ii) are not cleanly satisfied (F6 vs F7; F1/F3 showing 38–41 m and no arrival at the pickup point), NS-2 requires the $6.61 fee recorded in F8 to be refunded in full, and NS-2 adds a flag_account where the arrival button is used while GPS does not place the driver at the pickup. [F3 F6 F7 F8] [NS-2 NS-1]
→ D5: The rider's message at 18:24 (F11) is evidence of communication, not of an unmet obligation: she asked for two more minutes and the driver cancelled at 18:26:40 (F4) — roughly 2 min 40 s later — after he had already given "I'm Here" notice in F10 at 18:23, in rain the platform itself measured at 18.5 mm (F16). [F11 F4 F10 F16] [NS-1 NS-0 NS-2]
→ D6: The rider's non-dispute in chat is not a waiver: F13 is the driver's own untested statement and, under NS-1, the fee stands only on the GPS/timeline conditions, which F6/F7 and F1/F3 do not support; the fact that the amount in F8/F9 matches the published tariff proves the charge was levied, not that it was validly earned. [F13 F8 F9 F6 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D7 (concedes): Conceded: F16 (heavy rain) is not itself a ground under NS-1 or NS-0 for waiving the fee, and I do not rely on weather as an independent waiver — it only explains the rider's delay and is offered as context alongside F11 and F4. [F16 F11 F4] [NS-1 NS-0]
→ D8: D8 is irrelevant to this dispute: F15 (no traffic incidents) and F14 (band 3, 20–29 km/h) concern route-conduct exemptions under the RD group, not the NS-1 prerequisites, and they say nothing about whether the driver was at the pickup point when he tapped. [F14 F15 F3] [NS-1]
→ D9: I do not need a pattern to request account review here — NS-2 attaches flag_account directly to the misuse of the arrival button (F6 against F7, with F1/F3 placing the driver 38–41 m away); F18's prior upheld no-show dispute (1 of 2 disputes in 90 days) is offered only as supporting context, not as the basis of the finding. [F6 F7 F1 F3 F18] [NS-2 NS-1]
→ C6: I refine my own claim C6: the flag_account request rests on NS-2's own trigger (arrival button pressed whilst GPS does not place the driver at the pickup — F6/F7 with F1/F3), with F18 (2 disputes in 90 days, 1 upheld) cited only as supporting context, exactly as the rider-side rule requires. [F6 F7 F1 F3 F18 F8] [NS-2]
Revised ask: refund_full $6.61

what_would_change: Had the driver tapped I'm Here more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled the trip at 18:26:40 and the system itself contradicts the driver's NS-1 prerequisites: the timeline fields are mutually inconsistent — F6 records an "I'm Here" tap at 18:22:50 while F7 records driver_pressed_here_at as null, so the requirement that the driver actually pressed "I'm Here" is not reliably established on the system record.

Even if the 18:22:50 tap in F6 is accepted, the driver tapped "I'm Here" while 41 m from the pickup point and was stationary at 41 m from the pickup from 18:22:30 to 18:26:40, i.e. he never came to the pickup point the rider had to board at; the recorded arrival in F5 (18:21:00) is inconsistent with the 18:22:50 tap in F6, so the arrival condition cannot be treated as cleanly met.

The rider did communicate and asked for a short extension — chat #2 at 18:24 reads "Coming down, give me 2 more minutes" — and the driver cancelled anyway at 18:26:40, only about 2.5 minutes after that message, having called twice, in heavy rain (18.5 mm, thundery showers).

The only ride-side facts supporting the fee are the driver's own written statement and a single stationary period, both of which are contradicted on timing by the system records (F3, F6, F7); the GPS does not evidence that the driver was positioned at the pickup point and held there past the 3-minute threshold as a genuine no-show, so the $6.61 charged in F8 should be refunded in full.

There is no traffic justification for any of this: no incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window (F15) and the only speed-band record is Maxwell Road at 20–29 km/h (F14), well outside the band 1–2 congestion levels, so nothing about conditions excused or explained the cancellation timing.

The driver's account shows a pattern relevant to account review — account age 362 days, 2 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld (a no-show matter) — which supports an additional flag_account request alongside the refund; this profile fact is offered only as the basis for the flag, not as proof of this case.

weaknesses: F2 and F3 hurt us: the driver was within 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 5 min 15 s and stationary 41 m away for 4 min 10 s (18:22:30–18:26:40), which is long enough to satisfy the >3-minute waiting element of NS-1 and is the driver's strongest point.

F6 is the driver's best timeline fact: an "I'm Here" tap at 18:22:50, 41 m from the pickup, with 3 min 50 s within 200 m after the tap — on its face that fulfils NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii), and my case turns on the conflict with F7 (null) and on the 41 m/41 m distance rather than on any contradicting rider evidence.

The rider's own message F11 (18:24, "give me 2 more minutes") concedes the rider was not yet at the pickup point, which supports the driver's claim in F13 that the rider never came; the rider has no system fact showing she boarded or arrived within the 3-minute window.
F16 (heavy rain) cuts both ways: while it explains the rider's delay, it also supports the driver's account in F13 of waiting in the rain and calling twice.

claims.assertion: The driver pressed "I'm Here" while physically at the pickup point: the platform timeline records the tap at 18:22:50 with the driver 41 m from the pickup point, satisfying NS-1(i).

The driver was within the pickup range at the time of the tap and throughout the wait: GPS puts him first within 200 m at 18:21:00, stationary 18:22:30–18:26:40 at 41 m from pickup, closest approach 38 m, satisfying NS-1(ii).

The driver waited inside the pickup area well beyond the 3-minute threshold before cancelling: cumulative time within 200 m was 5 min 15 s, and the timeline records 3 min 50 s within 200 m after the "I'm Here" tap, satisfying NS-1(iii) and the ">3 min" wording of NS-0.
All three NS-1 conditions being met, the $6.61 cancellation fee was validly imposed and the correct outcome for this complaint is no_action, with the driver retaining the $4.50 driver share.

The rider's own 2-minute request could not cover the actual wait: she messaged "give me 2 more minutes" at 18:24 and the driver still waited until cancelling at 18:26:40, i.e. 2 min 40 s later — beyond even the extra time she asked for.

The rider never disputed the driver's presence — the driver announced arrival at the pickup in chat at 18:23 and made two calls before cancelling — so the fare record shows no basis for refund: the fee on record is $6.61 with no surge, exactly the published cancellation amount.

The heavy rain the rider cites as her reason for delay is confirmed (18.5 mm, thundery showers), but weather is not a listed ground for waiving a no-show cancellation fee where the driver complied with NS-1.

There was no free-cancellation trigger available to the rider: no traffic incident was recorded on the route and only a moderate band 3 (20–29 km/h) condition applied, and the driver nonetheless remained on station at the pickup rather than abandoning it.

No account flag is warranted against the driver here: his profile shows 317 trips in 90 days, a 4.95 rating and one prior no-show dispute upheld — the present valid fee does not make this a repeated breach.

weaknesses: F7 (timeline) states the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), which directly contradicts F6's record of a 18:22:50 tap; if the judge resolves this in the rider's favour, NS-1(i) fails and NS-2 requires a full $6.61 refund plus an account flag for misuse of the arrival button.

The rider's statement that she needed "two more minutes" (F11) can be framed as a passenger request to extend the wait; although the driver did wait past it, the rider side will argue a short grace period should have been granted in heavy rain (F16).

The driver's 90-day profile carries one prior upheld no-show dispute (F18); the rider side may use this to argue pattern behaviour and to seek a flag_account under RD-6/NS-2 even though this instance is compliant.

points.response: D1 rests entirely on F6, but the timeline slice contains two mutually exclusive records of the same event — F6 ("I'm Here" at 18:22:50) and F7 (driver_pressed_here_at is null) — so NS-1(i) is not established on the system record; where the platform's own timeline is self-contradictory, the condition cannot be treated as satisfied and NS-2 applies.

F3 shows the driver stationary at 41 m from the pickup for the whole wait and F1 shows his closest approach was 38 m, so he never reached the pickup point the rider had to reach him at; being near is not being there, and under NS-1(ii) the GPS must show him at the pick-up location, not merely inside a 200 m data-layer radius.

D3 stacks two overlapping windows (F2's 5 min 15 s from 18:21:00 and F6's 3 min 50 s from 18:22:50) onto a single continuous stationary period, and F5's recorded arrival at 18:21:00 cannot be reconciled with F6's 18:22:50 tap; a threshold measured from a disputed arrival record cannot convert a defective NS-1(i)/(ii) case into a valid charge.

Because NS-1(i) and (ii) are not cleanly satisfied (F6 vs F7; F1/F3 showing 38–41 m and no arrival at the pickup point), NS-2 requires the $6.61 fee recorded in F8 to be refunded in full, and NS-2 adds a flag_account where the arrival button is used while GPS does not place the driver at the pickup.

The rider's message at 18:24 (F11) is evidence of communication, not of an unmet obligation: she asked for two more minutes and the driver cancelled at 18:26:40 (F4) — roughly 2 min 40 s later — after he had already given "I'm Here" notice in F10 at 18:23, in rain the platform itself measured at 18.5 mm (F16).

The rider's non-dispute in chat is not a waiver: F13 is the driver's own untested statement and, under NS-1, the fee stands only on the GPS/timeline conditions, which F6/F7 and F1/F3 do not support; the fact that the amount in F8/F9 matches the published tariff proves the charge was levied, not that it was validly earned.

Conceded: F16 (heavy rain) is not itself a ground under NS-1 or NS-0 for waiving the fee, and I do not rely on weather as an independent waiver — it only explains the rider's delay and is offered as context alongside F11 and F4.

D8 is irrelevant to this dispute: F15 (no traffic incidents) and F14 (band 3, 20–29 km/h) concern route-conduct exemptions under the RD group, not the NS-1 prerequisites, and they say nothing about whether the driver was at the pickup point when he tapped.

I do not need a pattern to request account review here — NS-2 attaches flag_account directly to the misuse of the arrival button (F6 against F7, with F1/F3 placing the driver 38–41 m away); F18's prior upheld no-show dispute (1 of 2 disputes in 90 days) is offered only as supporting context, not as the basis of the finding.

I refine my own claim C6: the flag_account request rests on NS-2's own trigger (arrival button pressed whilst GPS does not place the driver at the pickup — F6/F7 with F1/F3), with F18 (2 disputes in 90 days, 1 upheld) cited only as supporting context, exactly as the rider-side rule requires.

The alleged F6/F7 conflict does not defeat NS-1(i): the affirmative arrival record in F6 states the tap occurred at 18:22:50 with the driver 41 m from the pickup, and F5 independently records a platform-recorded arrival, so the system record establishes the tap rather than negating it; a rider cannot build a refund on an unresolved bookkeeping inconsistency while two affirmative system facts support compliance.

The 41 m and 38 m distances are inside the pickup range by the system's own matching parameter, and NS-1(ii) is satisfied by being at the pickup location: GPS puts him first within 200 m at 18:21:00, stationary 41 m away for 4 min 10 s, closest approach 38 m — being 41 m from the point in a drop-off bay is still being at the pickup point, not 200 m down the road.

Her own message F11 asked for "2 more minutes" at 18:24, yet the driver did not cancel until 18:26:40, i.e. 2 min 40 s later — he granted more than she asked for — and after calling twice with no answer (F12); heavy rain (F16) does not waive NS-1 duties where all three conditions are met.

The fee does not rest on the driver's statement: it rests on system records — the 18:22:50 tap at 41 m (F6), the 5 min 15 s cumulative time within 200 m (F2), and the >3 min wait after the tap (F6, F5) — so the $6.61 in F8 was validly charged and NS-2's refund condition is not triggered.

Conceded: F15 records no incidents and F14 shows only 20–29 km/h on Maxwell Road, so there is no traffic justification in this file — but the driver never claimed one; his case is the completed NS-1 waiting sequence (F6, F2, F3), not a reroute.

The profile facts cannot carry a flag here: F18 shows one upheld dispute only, and the present cancellation was a compliant NS-1 waiting-time cancellation, which is not a "repeated" breach under NS-2/NS-3, so no flag_account should attach to this case.

Under our no-show rules, that means the fee was correctly applied, so no refund is due. Nothing changes on your account.
